problems.title: Three times another expression
problems.question: When is 4x−2 three times8−3x?
problems.idea: Translate the question into a standard algebraic or geometric relation.
steps: Thus13x=26, x=2.

problems.title: Maximum of a quadratic
problems.question: Find the largest value of 1+12x−9x².
problems.idea: Translate the question into a standard algebraic or geometric relation.
steps: The square is nonnegative, so the maximum is 5 at x=2/3.

problems.title: Divisor count after multiplying by10
problems.question: An integer ending in7 has 12 positive divisors. How many does ten times it have?
problems.idea: Translate the question into a standard algebraic or geometric relation.
formulas: The integer is divisible by neither2 nor5. Multiplication by 10 adds two new prime factors, each with exponent1.
steps: The divisor-count formula multiplies the old count by(1+1)²=4, so 12·4=48.

problems.title: Order powers of a negative fraction
problems.question: Order a, a², a³, a⁴ for a=1−√2.
problems.idea: Translate the question into a standard algebraic or geometric relation.
formulas: −1<a<0. Odd powers are negative, even powers positive, and magnitudes shrink with increasing exponent.
steps: Thus a<a³<a⁴<a².

problems.title: Odd integers in a set difference
problems.question: A=(3,10], B=(−1,5]. Count odd integers in B\A.
problems.idea: Translate the question into a standard algebraic or geometric relation.
steps: Its odd integers are 1 and 3.

problems.title: A radical of a product
problems.question: Simplify√[b(√a+√(a−b))(√a−√(a−b))] for b<0.
problems.idea: Translate the question into a standard algebraic or geometric relation.
formulas: The conjugate product is a−(a−b)=b.
steps: The whole radical is √b²=|b|=−b.
problems.note: The displayed inner radicals must also be real; in particular a≥0.

problems.title: An equiangular polygon
problems.question: Every interior angle of a polygon is 170°. Find the number of sides.
problems.idea: Translate the question into a standard algebraic or geometric relation.
formulas: Each exterior angle is 10°, and the exterior angles sum 360°.

problems.title: Equal lengths of a vector sum and difference
problems.question: Nonzero vectors satisfy|a+b|=|a−b|. Find their angle.
problems.idea: Translate the question into a standard algebraic or geometric relation.
formulas: Squaring gives|a|²+2a·b+|b|²=|a|²−2a·b+|b|².
steps: Thus a·b=0, and the angle is 90°.

problems.title: A composite polynomial
problems.question: f(x)=2x+1, g(x)=x²−t, and f(g(x))=2x²−3. Find t.
problems.idea: Translate the question into a standard algebraic or geometric relation.
steps: Compare constants:−2t+1=−3, so t=2.

problems.title: Minimum of a reciprocal sum
problems.question: Find the minimum of(4x+9)/√x.
problems.idea: Translate the question into a standard algebraic or geometric relation.
formulas: For u=√x>0, the expression is 4u+9/u≥2√36=12.
steps: Equality occurs at 4u=9/u, or u=3/2, x=9/4.

problems.title: A centroid triangle area
problems.question: Two medians of triangle ABC meet at K. If are a ABC=24, find are a BKC.
problems.idea: Translate the question into a standard algebraic or geometric relation.
formulas: The centroid is one third of the altitude from side BC.
steps: Both triangles have base BC, so are a BKC=24/3=8.

problems.title: Circle through three tangency points
problems.question: Three externally tangent circles have radii1,2,3. Find the radius of the circle through their contact points.
problems.idea: Translate the question into a standard algebraic or geometric relation.
formulas: The centres for m a 3–4–5 right triangle. Place them at(0,0),(3,0),(0,4).
steps: The contacts are(1,0),(0,1),(9/5,8/5). All are at distance 1 from(1,1).
Thus their circumcircle radius is 1.

problems.title: Count roots with a radical domain
problems.question: Count roots of(x²−17x)(199−x²)√(14−x)=0.
problems.idea: Translate the question into a standard algebraic or geometric relation.
formulas: The domain is x≤14. Candidate zeros are 0,17,±√199,14.
steps: Since√199>14, only 0,−√199,14 are allowed.

problems.title: Neighbouring diagonals of a regular polygon
problems.question: Find the angle between two neighbouring diagonals from one vertex of a regular n-gon, n≥5.
problems.idea: Translate the question into a standard algebraic or geometric relation.
formulas: They intercept one side’s arc of measure360°/n.
steps: The inscribed angle is half that arc, or 180°/n.

problems.title: Count sine-line intersections
problems.question: How many real roots has sinx=x/3?
problems.idea: Translate the question into a standard algebraic or geometric relation.
formulas: Any root has|x|≤3. The function h(x)=sinx−x/3 is odd.
steps: On(0,3), h″=−sinx<0, so h′ decreases strictly. Starting with h′(0)>0 and h(3)<0, the graph crosses0 exactly once after its maximum.
There is one positive root, its negative, and 0.

problems.title: Exclude both numerator roots
problems.question: For which a has(2x²−5x+2)/√(x−a)=0 no roots?
problems.idea: Translate the question into a standard algebraic or geometric relation.
formulas: The numerator roots are 1/2,2. The denominator requires x>a.
steps: Both are excluded exactly when a≥2.

problems.title: An odd auxiliary function
problems.question: g(x)=f(x)+x² is odd and f(−2)=3. Find f(2).
problems.idea: Translate the question into a standard algebraic or geometric relation.
formulas: g(−2)=3+4=7; oddness gives g(2)=−7.

problems.title: An even polynomial inequality
problems.question: Count integers n for which(n²−5)(n²−25)(n²−45)(n²−65)<0.
problems.idea: Translate the question into a standard algebraic or geometric relation.
formulas: The sign is negative when5<n²<25 or 45<n²<65.
steps: The integer roots are n=±3,±4,±7,±8. There are 8.

problems.title: A least common multiple plus a greatest common divisor
problems.question: Compute lcm(18,15)+gcd(48,45).
problems.idea: Translate the question into a standard algebraic or geometric relation.
steps: The sum is 93.

problems.title: Recover a function value
problems.question: Given f((x+2)/(5−x))=x/3, find f(1).
problems.idea: Translate the question into a standard algebraic or geometric relation.

problems.title: Secants to a diameter circle
problems.question: From C, secants meet the circle in D, A and M, B; AB is a diameter. If are a DCM:are a ACB=1:4, find∠CBD.
problems.idea: Translate the question into a standard algebraic or geometric relation.
formulas: Thales gives BD⊥CA and AM⊥CB. Thus D, M are the altitude feet of triangle ACB.
steps: If θ=∠ACB, then CD=CB cosθ and CM=CA cosθ. The common included-angle are a formula gives are a ratio cos²θ=1/4.
With C outside,θ is acute, so θ=60°. Because BD⊥CA,∠CBD=90°−θ=30°.

problems.title: Cancel a large geometric term
problems.question: A geometric progression has b₁=1, b₂=2. Find(b₂₀₂₄+b₂₀₂₂)/(b₂₀₂₄−b₂₀₂₂).
problems.idea: Translate the question into a standard algebraic or geometric relation.
formulas: b₂₀₂₄=4b₂₀₂₂.
steps: Cancel b₂₀₂₂ to get(4+1)/(4−1)=5/3.

problems.title: An infinite geometric series
problems.question: FindΣ from n=1 to∞ of(−1/2)ⁿ.
problems.idea: Translate the question into a standard algebraic or geometric relation.
formulas: The first term is −1/2 and ratio−1/2, whose magnitude is<1.

problems.title: A point on an absolute-value graph
problems.question: The graph y=|x−1|+3ᵃ passes through(−2,6). Find a.
problems.idea: Translate the question into a standard algebraic or geometric relation.
formulas: Substitute:6=|−3|+3ᵃ.
steps: Thus3ᵃ=3 and a=1.

problems.title: A number and its preceding even numbers
problems.question: Find a natural number equal to one seventh the sum of all smaller positive even integers.
problems.idea: Translate the question into a standard algebraic or geometric relation.
formulas: For an even N=2k, the sum is 2+4+…+2(k−1)=k(k−1).
steps: Then14k=k(k−1), so k=15, N=30. For odd N=2k+1, the equation k(k+1)=7(2k+1) has discriminant197, not a square, so no integer k.

problems.title: Graphs with absolute values and domains
problems.question: For which f do graphs f(|x|) and|f(x)| differ: x,1/x², x³,√x?
problems.idea: Translate the question into a standard algebraic or geometric relation.
formulas: For f=√x, f(|x|)=√|x| is defined for all real x, whereas|f(x)|=√x is defined only for x≥0.
steps: The other three functions give matching expressions on matching domains.

problems.title: A finite geometric sum
problems.question: Compute1+1/2+…+(1/2)¹².
problems.idea: Translate the question into a standard algebraic or geometric relation.
steps: Simplify to 2−(1/2)¹².

problems.title: A section point and a midpoint vector
problems.question: In OAB, AC:CB=2:1 and K is midpoint OC. Express OK in a=OA, b=OB.
problems.idea: Translate the question into a standard algebraic or geometric relation.
steps: Halving gives OK=a/6+b/3.

problems.title: Sum of strings of nines
problems.question: aₙ has n digits9. Find a₁+…+a₁₀₀.
problems.idea: Translate the question into a standard algebraic or geometric relation.

problems.title: A trigonometric maximum
problems.question: Count roots of √3sinx+cosx=2 on[0,2π].
problems.idea: Translate the question into a standard algebraic or geometric relation.
formulas: The left side is 2sin(x+π/6).
steps: Its maximum 2 is attained when x+π/6=π/2+2kπ. Only x=π/3 lies in the stated interval.

problems.title: Solve for two vectors
problems.question: a−2b=−5i and a+b=4i+3j. Find the angle between a, b.
problems.idea: Translate the question into a standard algebraic or geometric relation.
steps: Their dot product is 5, and lengths are √5,√10. Thus cosθ=5/√50=1/√2.

problems.title: A secant split into equal pieces
problems.question: A tangent from an external point has length √2. A secant’s outside and inside pieces are equal. Find whole secant length.
problems.idea: Translate the question into a standard algebraic or geometric relation.
formulas: If each piece is t, the secant power is t·2t=(√2)²=2.
steps: Thus t=1 and whole length 2t=2.

problems.title: Equal sums in an arithmetic progression
problems.question: A nonconstant arithmetic progression satisfies a₃+aₙ=a₁+a₁₁. Find n.
problems.idea: Translate the question into a standard algebraic or geometric relation.
formulas: Use aⱼ=a₁+(j−1)d, d≠0.

problems.title: Four areas cut by three cevians
problems.question: A right triangle has legs1,3. Its altitude, bisector, and median from the right vertex split its are a into4 parts. Find the ratio from the shorter-leg side.
problems.idea: Translate the question into a standard algebraic or geometric relation.
formulas: On the hypotenuse, the altitude foot is at fraction1²/(1²+3²)=1/10 from the shorter-leg endpoint. The bisector is at fraction1/(1+3)=1/4; the median at 1/2.
steps: The four hypotenuse fractions are 1/10,3/20,1/4,1/2. Triangles sharing the vertex have areas proportional to them.
Multiply by 20 to get2:3:5:10.

problems.title: Divide a trigonometric quotient by cosine
problems.question: Find(3sinx−cosx)/(3cosx−sinx) if tanx=2.
problems.idea: Translate the question into a standard algebraic or geometric relation.
formulas: Divide numerator and denominator by cosx.
steps: The result is(3tanx−1)/(3−tanx)=(6−1)/(3−2)=5.

problems.title: Minimum of tangent-square and cotangent-square terms
problems.question: Find the minimum of 20tan²x+45cot²(−x).
problems.idea: Translate the question into a standard algebraic or geometric relation.
formulas: Let t=tan²x>0. Since cot²(−x)=1/t, the expression is 20t+45/t≥2√900.
steps: The minimum is 60, at t=3/2.

problems.title: Squared sum from a fixed separation
problems.question: Two real numbers are 10 apart. Which listed squared sum 16,28,54,42 can occur?
problems.idea: Translate the question into a standard algebraic or geometric relation.
steps: Only 54 is at least50, and it occurs when x+y=±√8 with x−y=10.

problems.title: Circumradius of an isosceles trapezoid
problems.question: A trapezoid has bases2,8 and legs5. Find its circumradius.
problems.idea: Translate the question into a standard algebraic or geometric relation.
formulas: Height=√(5²−3²)=4. Place the base vertices at(±4,0),(±1,4); centre is(0, k).
steps: Equating radii gives 16+k²=1+(4−k)², so k=1/8. Radius=√(16+1/64)=5√41/8.

problems.title: Hexagon-to-square area ratio
problems.question: A regular hexagon is inscribed in a circle and a square circumscribes that circle. Find their are a ratio.
problems.idea: Translate the question into a standard algebraic or geometric relation.
formulas: With radius R, the hexagon side is R, are a 3√3R²/2. The square side is 2R, are a 4R².
steps: Their ratio is 3√3/8.

problems.title: Two roots within a monotone sine interval
problems.question: For which a does cos²x+(2a+3)sinx−a²=0 have exactly 2 roots on[0,π/2]?
problems.idea: Translate the question into a standard algebraic or geometric relation.
formulas: Put t=sinx∈[0,1], a one-to-one substitution. The concave quadratic is g(t)=1−t²+(2a+3)t−a².
steps: Two distinct roots in[0,1] require a vertex inside the interval, nonpositive endpoint values, and positive discriminant. These give−3/2<a<−1/2,|a|≥1,2a+3−a²≤0, and 12a+13>0.
Combining yields−13/12<a≤−1. At a=−1, the two roots are endpoints t=0,1; at a=−13/12 they merge and are excluded.

problems.title: A cyclist meeting two walkers
problems.question: A cyclist leaves A for B as two equal-speed walkers leave B in opposite directions. He meets the approaching walker after18 min and catches the other 1 hour after passing B. Find his A-to-B time.
problems.idea: Translate the question into a standard algebraic or geometric relation.
formulas: Let T be that time in hours, and r=walker speed/cyclist speed. The first meeting gives T/(1+r)=0.3. The later catch gives r=1/(T+1).
steps: Substitute:T=0.3(1+1/(T+1)), or 10T²+7T−6=0. The positive root is T=1/2.
